analysis.title: AI's "Most Bullish Chart" Is A Credit Crunch In Disguise: GPU Rents Soar As Lenders Slash Advance Rates From 80% To 50%
key_insights: Rising GPU rental indices (Silicon Data B200 up 23.5% from end of August to Nov 19, $5.62 to $6.94 per GPU-hour, H100 up 67% since July 2025) are argued to reflect tighter credit rather than stronger end demand.

Per Stanley Lee of Liquid Compute, the spot bid includes buyers who want term contracts but cannot get them because neoclouds cannot get chips financed by lenders. Spot pricing reflects buyers' cost of capital as much as demand.

Lender LTVs on neocloud GPU loans fell from 80% over the summer to 70% after Labor Day and now 50-60%, with 50% structures quoted in the mid-to-high teens. On a $100M cluster, the cash needed outside the senior loan rose from $30M to up to $50M, a 67% increase.

Many small neoclouds funded the equity gap with customer prepayments, and those customers rely on VC money. VCs deployed about 25% less in Q3 than Q1. Lee: access to debt equals access to equity in the middle market.

Private credit now underwrites operator and offtaker separately, sees five to ten loans a week backed by the same few AI companies, and refuses first or second deployments. The article compares this to subprime correlation and calls the paper Collateralized Chip Obligations.
Buyers pay about $33,000 more per B300 over three years to avoid a roughly $35,000 deposit, implying a 30-55% annual rate on the prepayment. This shows how stretched startup cash is.

The market is thin. Bernstein found four H100 quotes of $3.50, $3.30, $3.01 and $2.80 on the same day, a 25% spread, against CoreWeave's assumed $3.81. The Ornn H100 index fell from about $3.50 in early November to $2.92.

Private credit funds are asking Liquid Compute for indicative prices on put options on its B300 rental index, 1-3 calls a day for two weeks, versus none six months ago. This signals demand for residual-value hedges.

Token prices are falling while GPU rents rise. Ornn's OpenAI token index fell from above $1.20 to $0.31 and its Anthropic index from about $2.00 to $0.77 since July. Nvidia said token prices are down nearly 60% since May, which implies a margin squeeze for GPU renters absent throughput gains.

Bull rebuttals: Goldman cites OpenRouter token volumes up 35x year on year, Hopper re-contracted at about 2x original price, B300 rates up over 60% since launch. Wells Fargo cites Oracle 97.9% AI infrastructure utilization and 20% renewal premiums. Silicon Data's Carmen Li notes her indices include term contracts.

Rents hit a record while CoreWeave CDS widened to about 1,300bp, its 2031 notes yielded 16%, and hedge funds went underweight AI for the first time since 2023. The article says credit is the market with money at risk and sides with credit over the chart.
Goldman's Privorotsky now says oversupply, not power or permitting, is the key medium-term risk, as efficiency gains compress per-token inference costs.

Goldman credit strategists expect $320B of chip and compute financing in 2027, almost 7x this year's pace. Spreads run 150-240bp for IG chip deals vs about 100bp ordinary IG, and up to 775bp for leveraged deals. Much of it depends on residual-value guarantees, historically from Nvidia, which has $118B of guarantees outstanding.

Nvidia interim CEO Kress said Nvidia will remain supportive of neoclouds but more selective. Kedrosky calls the system fractional reserve banking with one bank, and says $10T of capex needs $3-6T of annual revenue by 2032.
Two-phase thesis: now, credit-starved buyers bid up short-dated capacity as fewer clusters get funded. Later, VC funding slows, operators default, and foreclosed clusters get re-let into weak demand.

market_movers.rationale: CDS around 1,300bp and 2031 notes at a 16% yield. Bernstein questioned its $10B/yr re-renting claim, which assumed $3.81 H100 vs $2.80-3.50 market quotes.
Rothschild Redburn's Haissl put Sell ratings on CoreWeave and Nebius in September, citing VC-funded customer demand.
Nvidia's backstops and guarantees ($118B outstanding) support the neocloud financing ecosystem and it is turning more selective.
Wells Fargo cites 97.9% AI infrastructure utilization and 20% renewal premiums as the bull data point.

sector_views.rationale: Rising rents reflect credit scarcity. Advance rates are falling, spreads are wide, and demand depends on VC funding.

crypto_views: Many mid-market neocloud borrowers are converted bitcoin miners.
risk_factors: A thin spot market where few bids hitting could drop the floor in rental indices.
VC funding slowdown cutting buyers' ability to pay.
Lender foreclosures and re-letting of GPU clusters into weaker demand.
Withdrawal of Nvidia backstops and residual-value guarantees.
Token price deflation and efficiency gains outpacing demand growth.
Correlated offtaker concentration in a handful of AI companies.

tension_points.bull_case: Rising rents signal scarcity. Goldman cites 35x OpenRouter token volume growth, Hopper re-contracted at 2x, and Wells Fargo cites Oracle 97.9% utilization.
tension_points.bear_case: Rents are rising because credit is tightening. Lenders cut LTVs to 50-60%, buyers cannot get term deals, demand depends on VC funding, and token prices are down over 50%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Neocloud compute bills shown to be paid mostly from customer revenue rather than the last equity round, or credit spreads and CoreWeave CDS tightening alongside rising rents.

theme_stances.key_argument: Rising rental prices mostly reflect lenders pulling back and buyers shut out of term contracts, not healthy end demand.
theme_stances.evidence: We'd go with credit over the chart.
